conventions.convention: The fundamental form is ω(v,w)=g(Jv,w); the complex orientation has positive frame (v₁,Jv₁,…,vₙ,Jvₙ), and dV=ωⁿ/n!. On cotangent forms J acts by pullback, so Je=-f and Jf=e.

The Hodge star extends complex-linearly, the integral Hermitian pairing is linear in its first variable, ε(k)=(-1)^(k(k-1)/2), and the Weil operator C acts by i^(p-q). A polarization has positive definite Hermitian form h(x,y)=Q(Cx,ȳ).
Full AC is assumed in the geometric and analytic results. The orthogonal-splitting argument and two-plane example are choice-free.

Analytification uses smooth projective complex schemes of pure dimension n≥0. Dimension zero gives a finite discrete set; the empty scheme has empty analytification. In these cases η_A=0 and positivity is vacuous.
Morphisms, direct sums and short exact sequences in the definition concern rational pure Hodge structures of one fixed weight k.

Λ on cohomology acts on the unique harmonic representative, not on an arbitrary closed form. For 0≤k≤n, Pᵏ=ker L^(n-k+1); rationality requires the Kähler class to be the real image of a rational class.
For k≤n, Q_k(a,b)=ε(k)∫a∧b∧ω^(n-k). The full-cohomology polarization S_k restricts to (-1)^r Q_k on LʳP^(k-2r); higher degrees use transport from the complementary degree with Tate shift.

Extension to an arbitrary characteristic-zero field preserves the supplied rational matrix identities and decompositions; it asserts neither positivity over that field nor rational descent of its new subobjects.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. A smooth projective complex scheme X of pure dimension n≥0 has compact Hausdorff second-countable analytification, with the stated zero-dimensional and empty conventions. Every ample invertible sheaf A has a positive closed real (1,1)-form η_A satisfying J[η_A]=ρ(c₁(A)). Morphisms between smooth separated finite-type complex schemes of pure dimensions induce holomorphic maps.

Assume AC. On a compact Kähler n-fold, L^(n-k):Hᵏ(X;ℝ)→H^(2n-k)(X;ℝ) is an isomorphism for 0≤k≤n. Harmonic representatives transport the Lefschetz sl₂ action and primitive decomposition to cohomology. If [ω] is the real image of a rational class, the decompositions and L-isomorphisms are rational and persist over every characteristic-zero field.

Assume AC. For a compact Kähler n-fold and 0≤k≤n, Q_k is (-1)^k-symmetric and type-orthogonal on Pᵏ, and i^(p-q)Q_k(a,ā)=(n-k)!‖a_harm‖²>0 for nonzero a∈P^(p,q). At rational Kähler classes it is a rational polarization; the sign-adjusted primitive direct sum polarizes full cohomology. Positivity and nondegeneracy hold at every real Kähler class, and primitive kernels vary continuously along continuous Kähler families.

For a polarized rational pure Hodge structure (V,Q) and rational sub-Hodge structure U, Q|_U is a polarization and V=U⊕U⊥_Q is an orthogonal Hodge direct sum with polarized complement. Every short exact sequence of polarizable rational pure Hodge structures of a fixed weight splits, and every polarizable structure is a finite direct sum of simple structures. The supplied rational splitting identities persist after characteristic-zero scalar extension, without positivity or descent assertions there.

Assume AC. A smooth projective complex variety of pure dimension n with chosen ample line class has finite-dimensional functorial rational pure Hodge cohomology, rational hard Lefschetz, primitive Hodge–Riemann positivity, a sign-adjusted full-cohomology polarization and orthogonal splitting of rational Hodge substructures. Absolute positivity and hard Lefschetz hold for real Kähler classes, primitive kernels vary continuously along Kähler families, and rational splittings and isomorphisms persist over characteristic-zero fields. The package does not supply relative hard Lefschetz or semisimplicity of arbitrary local systems.

published_dependencies.used_for: Standing full-choice hypothesis inherited through the algebraic, analytic and comparison suppliers.
Complex connections, Hermitian compatibility and rank-one local connection calculations in the Fubini–Study construction.
Compactness, Hausdorffness, second-countability and standard holomorphic charts of projective space.
Curvature convention in the explicit Hermitian line connection.
The normalization -Ω/(2πi) represents the real image of the integral first Chern class.
c₁(A⊗d)=d c₁(A), applied componentwise after checking numerability and CW homotopy type.
A power of an ample line bundle gives a closed projective embedding with pullback of O(1) equal to that power.
Local graph coordinates from standard smooth algebraic presentations when both coordinate blocks have positive dimension.
The zero-dimensional smooth-presentation case and local holomorphic coordinate inversion.
Standard smooth presentations with an invertible Jacobian minor and relative dimension m-r.
Closed points of finite-type complex affine schemes have residue field ℂ.
Existence of a maximal ideal in a nonzero affine coordinate ring under AC.
Algebraic closedness of ℂ in the closed-point identification.
Affine quotient presentations of projective embeddings and diagonals; their complex point loci are closed polynomial zero sets.
Closed scheme diagonals in the Hausdorffness argument for noncompact analytifications.
Paracompact Hausdorff CGWH and CW homotopy-type hypotheses, plus numerability, needed for tensor-power Chern additivity.
Independence of the Hodge–Riemann integral from closed representatives on compact boundaryless manifolds.
Full AC supplies the countable-choice hypothesis of Stokes and the analytic comparison suppliers.
The two-plane star table *e=f, *f=-e and its complex-linear extension.

concerns.concern: The Statement says, “Every standard smooth algebraic chart of X becomes a holomorphic chart of X^{an}.” Proof 1.1 establishes holomorphic coordinate charts only after shrinking to local analytic graph neighbourhoods. A whole standard smooth affine presentation need not be a single holomorphic coordinate chart: on the smooth projective elliptic curve y²=x³-x, the affine open y≠0 has standard smooth presentation ℂ[x,y,1/y]/(y²-x³+x), since 2y is invertible. Its free-coordinate projection x is not injective, and its analytification is a punctured genus-one surface, not an open subset of ℂ. The global chart clause therefore needs explicit local shrinking; the remaining analytification and Kähler-form arguments do not require that stronger clause.

alerts.finding: F1 repeats “every standard smooth algebraic chart becomes a holomorphic chart.” The cited analytification proof supplies local analytic graph neighbourhoods, not a single coordinate chart on every standard smooth affine open. The standard smooth open ℂ[x,y,1/y]/(y²-x³+x) of a projective elliptic curve is a counterexample to the global wording. The consumer's submersion construction uses local coordinates, so that local qualification suffices.

F1 says “every standard smooth algebraic chart becomes a holomorphic chart.” This repeats the overbroad global-chart clause of the analytification supplier. A standard smooth affine open of an elliptic curve, such as ℂ[x,y,1/y]/(y²-x³+x), requires local analytic shrinking and is not itself a holomorphic coordinate chart. The modification proof needs only the resulting manifold structure and holomorphic morphisms.

seams_checked.note: Checked the conventions, scalar comparison, top-integral comparison, exterior Lefschetz/star identity, Kähler commutators and harmonic Hodge theorem. The consumers preserve AC, degree ranges, primitive kernels, type shifts and rational-class qualifications.
At n=k=1 the cited primitive-star formula gives *u=-iu; the basis calculation and density u∧*ū=2e∧f agree with the supplier's orientation and normalization.

The modification lemma and logarithmic theorem use compact smooth projective analytifications and pure functorial Hodge theory on compact strata, treating empty and differing-dimensional components separately. The modification lemma repeats the supplier's defective global-chart wording, recorded in alerts.

The family lemma correctly uses fibrewise primitive/sign-adjusted polarizations, and the fixed-part proof applies rational hard Lefschetz separately by relative dimension. Local-system conclusions use additional family and fixed-part arguments. The family lemma repeats the supplier's defective global-chart wording, recorded in alerts.

The proper-weights theorem uses smooth projective analytification and pure Hodge theory componentwise on hypercover terms. Differential strictness is separately derived from Hodge–de Rham degeneration rather than imported as an unsupported conclusion of analytification.

Checked the point-image induction base, real Kähler hypotheses for L+εη, the middle limiting-primitive lemma and polarized sub-Hodge restrictions in Construction F. These uses retain the classical first-slot Weil convention and sign changes. Relative and local-system conclusions invoke additional suppliers and constructions.
